title: Intro to Body Awareness 🤸🏿‍♀️ A Simple Dance Warm Up to Loosen Up and Connect to your Body

method.teacher_system: The teacher guides the learner through a series of body-part-specific movements, starting from the face and moving down to the legs. She encourages the learner to observe sensations and release tension through breath and gentle, rhythmic movement. The lesson concludes with an improvisational segment to integrate the body awareness.
method.signature: The teacher explicitly frames the dance as a way to shift attention from the mind to the body, using the metaphor of a paintbrush to guide movement.

practices.what: The teacher instructs the learner to softly massage their face to increase oxygen levels and relax muscles.
The teacher guides the learner through head rolls while observing the environment to shift attention to the present.
The teacher leads shoulder shrugs and rolls, emphasizing exhaling to release tension.
The teacher demonstrates brushing the shoulders from side to side to release accumulated stress.
The teacher extends the brushing movement to the arms and hands, encouraging the learner to feel the movement.
The teacher guides the learner to shake out their hands.
The teacher instructs the learner to move their chest in and out to improve posture and circulation.
The teacher uses the imagery of a paintbrush in the center of the chest to guide circular movements.
The teacher guides the learner to roll the abdominal area to stretch the digestive organs.
The teacher leads a wave-like movement with the upper body, starting from the head.
The teacher encourages the learner to improvise, focusing on the upper body and connecting to the music.
The teacher invites the learner to run around the room or in place to let go and shake out the body.

adaptations.difficulty: Feeling tension during the back movement.
adaptations.adjustment: Adjust the intensity of the movement or breathe more deeply.

adaptations.difficulty: Not having enough space to run around.

beliefs.belief: The first step to being present is to observe sensations in the body without judging oneself.

feelings.response: The teacher acknowledges that the learner may feel tingling or tension and encourages them to simply observe it.

struggles.theme: Feeling stiff and lacking confidence in movement
Struggling with perfectionism and focusing on choreography

clicked.theme: The teacher's encouragement to not worry about how one looks
The focus on releasing tension and body awareness

meant.theme: Feeling free, connected, and emotionally released

method.limits: The video does not show the feet clearly in all segments, and the teacher's instructions are primarily focused on the upper body, which may limit the learner's understanding of full-body coordination.
